headline: Sea Turtle Eggs Laid on California Beaches for First Time
meta_description: Olive ridley sea turtles have nested naturally on the US West Coast for the first time ever, marking a significant milestone for the species.
summary_short: Olive ridley sea turtles have laid eggs on California beaches in a historic first for the West Coast. The tiny turtles typically live in tropical waters worldwide.
body:
Sea turtles have nested naturally on California beaches for the first time ever recorded on the US West Coast. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's West Coast Fisheries division announced the milestone discovery on Facebook.

The eggs belong to olive ridley turtles, the smallest of all sea turtle species. Adult olive ridleys typically weigh up to 100 pounds. Though found worldwide, these turtles primarily inhabit the tropical waters of the Pacific, Indian, and Atlantic oceans—making their appearance and nesting on the West Coast an unexpected and welcome sign.

The discovery represents a rare moment in marine conservation, suggesting changing ocean conditions or expanding ranges for a species that has faced decades of pressure from human activity and habitat loss.
quick_facts: First-ever natural sea turtle nesting recorded on US West Coast
Olive ridley turtles: smallest sea turtle species, up to 100 pounds
Primarily found in tropical Pacific, Indian, and Atlantic oceans
